content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce initial forecast peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment drops sharply (e.g., <0.4) — adjust downward bias by +2–5% of recent mean.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.1x recent 5-day average.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged overreaction: if sentiment is high but price drops 3+ days later, forecast should be 1–2% below true outcome for next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle — reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 3+ days, suppress forecast volatility — cap range within ±1.5% of recent 7-day mean.
